analysis.title: Americas Investment Banks: Exiting 3Q26, back to mid-cycle - top-line growth continues, but valuation appears mostly fair
key_insights: Independent investment bank (IBank) stocks rose ~13% on average from 10/21/26 (the day before the first 3Q26 print, ex-JEF) and beat the S&P 500 by 16pp. GS says the move was entirely multiple rerating, driven by a 6% median earnings beat (higher revenue, lower expenses) and fading late-cycle fears.

GS sees the cycle as mid-cycle and sees limited further rerating. The group trades at ~16.0x GSe NTM P/E (15.5x consensus), about the 55th percentile of the past decade. IBank multiples typically peak early in the cycle.

YTD announced industry M&A volume is up ~25% YoY. Strategic/large-cap volume is up ~40% and sponsor/mid-cap is -5%/+15%. 3Q26 restructuring advisory was up 5% YoY and YTD annualized secondaries capital raised is down ~30% YoY.

Theme 1: the non-M&A advisory outlook is constructive, especially restructuring. Secondaries plus restructuring were an estimated 18% of 2025 IBank revenue. Drivers are the 2028/29 debt maturity walls, higher rates, tighter financing (financial distress at some frontier AI companies), rising bankruptcy filings and AI disruption in software.

Restructuring revenue has a 40% R-squared to the Fed funds level. GS forecasts 2026E group restructuring revenue roughly flat after a strong 2025, then +6% in 2027E. The forward curve now prices ~3 hikes by end-2027 versus 2 cuts at the start of 2026.

Secondaries: structural tailwinds (more GPs and LPs using them) and cyclical ones (PE exit constraints push firms toward continuation funds). 59% of PE unrealized value is 5+ years aged versus a 50% average, which raises LP pressure on GPs to return capital. Valuation gaps (85%) and asset competition (70%) are the top deployment constraints in the Secondaries Investor survey.

Theme 2: M&A remains mid-cycle. Volumes are up ~85% this cycle, leaving ~70-80pp of growth (~80-90pp excluding AI-related deals, where growth so far is ~75%). GS's regression model forecasts 17% NTM global M&A volume growth, with US at 19%.

Strategic/large-cap M&A is strong. Management teams cite backlog replenishment, and GS sees a possible further wave through end-2028, perhaps accelerated by Democratic midterm success and a more active antitrust posture. Strategic volumes are at 4.8% of equal-weight global market cap versus a 6.7% average, while large-cap is at 2.2% versus 1.9%, the first time above average since 2021. Average deal size is up ~20% YoY.

Sponsor/mid-cap M&A is the weak spot. Sponsors are 27% of YTD volume versus 35% on the 5-year average, and Sept/Oct sponsor volume fell more than 45% YoY after +9% in August. Sponsor M&A has a -38% correlation to short-term rate changes versus -27% for strategic, and the forward curve prices Fed funds ~90bps higher at end-2026 than at the start of the year. GS still expects measured growth from LP pressure and aged capital.

Theme 3: Dealogic M&A fees captured only ~50% of IBank advisory revenue in 3Q26, versus over 80% a decade ago and a 56% average. Non-M&A advisory revenue is up ~305% since 1Q17. The rolling 12-quarter R-squared of reported advisory revenue to Dealogic fees fell to 76% from 95% in 1Q22, which lowers earnings forecastability.

Theme 4: operating leverage is modest. GS sees median 2026E pre-tax margin up only ~10bps YoY, ~100bps below the 2017-19 average. It sees 180bps and 90bps of expansion in 2027E and 2028E. Structural comp leverage is negative (comp ratios 63.4%/62.3%/61.5% in 2026E/27E/28E) and 2026E non-comp dollar growth is forecast at 10% versus 8% at the start of 2026, driven by AI/data subscriptions and travel. 3Q26 non-comp expense was 3% below the Street.
Mid-cap-skewed IBanks (HLI, PIPR) are preferred for margin sustainability because of more variable comp structures and less reliance on fixed guarantees and deferred stock.

Theme 5: IBank cash balances are up ~90% over 2023-26E, with a further ~10% expected by 2028E. 3Q26 gross buybacks rose ~30% YoY, JEF raised its repurchase authorization and PIPR announced a new one. GS sees room for opportunistic buybacks and inorganic growth.

Top picks are EVR, LCLN, PIPR and PJT (all Buy), favoured for structural growth and non-M&A advisory exposure. EVR and PJT are best positioned for restructuring, secondaries and large-cap M&A. EVR's secondaries share is 14% of 2025 revenue versus 5% for the group, and PJT's restructuring/secondaries share is 35%/16% versus 9%/5% for peers.

Estimate and target changes: 2026E/28E IBank EPS estimates fall 2%/1%, Q5-Q8 target P/Es rise 0.6x on average, and 12-month price targets rise 3% on average. GS projects 10% upside plus a 3% dividend yield, for a 13% total return. FCN's target P/E rises 2.0x because GS sees it turning the corner on company-specific concerns.
Ratings: Buy on EVR, PJT, PIPR, JEF, HLI and LCLN. Neutral on MC and FCN. Sell on PWP and LAZ.

market_movers.rationale: Quality compounder with the most diversified revenue mix and strong sponsor and secondaries build-out. YTD completions are up 26% YoY and backlogs are up 195% since 1Q23. GSe 2026E/27E/28E EPS are 3%/2%/5% above the Street. Target unchanged, 21% upside.
Best-in-class exposure to large-cap strategic M&A, restructuring and secondaries, with low net income volatility. Target raised from $180 and target P/E raised to 19.5x from 19.0x. 20% upside.
Diversified model with acyclical trading revenue and a more variable comp structure. It trades at ~13.5x GSe NTM P/E (~70th percentile) and GS sees further rerating potential. 17% upside.
Faster growth from smaller scale, senior banker hiring, and leverage to mid-cap and sponsor M&A. Target raised from $29.50 and P/E to 17.5x from 17.0x. 15% upside.
Target raised from $164 and P/E to 19.0x from 18.5x. HLI is named as best positioned for margin sustainability. Total return 17%.
Target raised from $52 and P/E to 11.0x from 10.0x. JEF raised its share repurchase authorization. Total return 20%.
Target raised from $62 with the P/E held at 15.5x. Risks are lower completions and greater normalization of sponsor M&A.
Target raised from $169 and target P/E raised 2.0x to 15.5x because GS sees idiosyncratic business concerns easing and potentially acyclical growth. Implied return is -2%.
Target cut from $14. EPS estimates are cut 3%/5% for 2026E/27E. Implied total return is -3%.
Target raised from $35 on a 1.0x higher P/E (10.5x). 4Q26E EPS is cut 50% and 2026E EPS 21%. Implied total return is -1%.

sector_views.rationale: Top-line growth continues with M&A mid-cycle and constructive restructuring and secondaries, but valuation is mostly fair after the rerating. GS prefers structural-growth names with non-M&A exposure (EVR, LCLN, PIPR, PJT).

earnings_insights: 3Q26 IBank median EPS was 6% above Visible Alpha consensus (6% above GSe), on revenue 1% above consensus and operating margin ~115bps above consensus. Median revenue growth was 3% QoQ and 10% YoY, and median EPS growth was 28% QoQ and 1% YoY.

3Q26 reported EPS vs consensus: PWP +132%, EVR +70%, LCLN +23%, HLI +12%, JEF +6%, PJT +6%, MC +4%, PIPR -7%, FCN -11%, LAZ -14%. Revenue vs consensus was: PWP +37%, EVR +32%, LCLN +11%, HLI +9%, LAZ -6%.
3Q26 median advisory revenue was +14% QoQ and +14% YoY, in line with GSe. Median comp ratio was flat QoQ and -41bps YoY, and non-comp ratio was 136bps below consensus.
Management tone on 4Q26 and 2027 M&A and on restructuring was constructive. EVR guided to continued advisory strength after YTD advisory fees up 42% YoY, and highlighted 60 sponsor coverage bankers.
3Q26 gross buybacks were up ~30% YoY across IBanks.

macro_indicators.reading: ~3 rate hikes priced by end of 2027 vs. 2 cuts priced at the start of 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied higher rates are cited as a headwind to sponsor M&A and a support for restructuring demand.

macro_indicators.reading: Priced ~90bps higher than at the start of 2026 (EOP rate 3.64% as of 1/2/26 vs 4.57% current)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher short rates weigh on sponsor M&A, which has a -38% correlation to rate changes, and on valuations that PE buyers can pay.

macro_indicators.reading: Priced ~90bps higher than at the start of 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Raises financing costs for leveraged deals, so sponsor M&A growth is expected to be measured.
Supports the view that M&A is mid-cycle with growth continuing.

trade_ideas.rationale: Diversified quality compounder with strong sponsor and secondaries growth and backlogs up 195% since 1Q23.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker M&A backlogs, longer time to completions, higher compensation expense, longer-term share losses.

trade_ideas.rationale: Best-in-class large-cap strategic M&A, restructuring and secondaries exposure with low earnings volatility.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker M&A backlogs, slower scaling, inability to drive margin catch-up.

trade_ideas.rationale: Diversified model with acyclical trading revenue and a variable comp structure, with room to rerate.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower IBanking and trading growth, weaker backlogs, large cash build dragging on returns.

trade_ideas.rationale: Faster revenue growth than peers (13% vs 12% 2026E-28E CAGR) from senior banker hiring and leverage to mid-cap and sponsor M&A.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower M&A, continued slowdown in mid-cap and sponsor M&A, longer acquisition integration.

risk_factors: Weaker M&A backlogs leading to lower revenue expectations, and longer time to completions pushing out M&A and restructuring revenue.
Sponsor and mid-cap M&A stays subdued because of valuation gaps and higher rates.
Higher compensation expense and a continued rise in non-comp spend pressure margins.
Restructuring and large-cap M&A weakness (FCN risk) and a US recession weighing on IBanking (JEF risk).
Limited further rerating: the group is already at ~55th percentile P/E after a 13% rally.
geopolitical: US midterm election: Democratic success could presage a more active antitrust posture, which GS says could pull forward large-cap strategic M&A ahead of a potentially more onerous antitrust backdrop.

tension_points.bull_case: Constructive management commentary on 4Q26 and 2027 M&A, a possible further wave of large-cap strategic M&A through 2028, restructuring upside and 17% forecast NTM M&A volume growth leave 70-80pp of cycle growth.
tension_points.bear_case: After a 13% rally driven entirely by multiple rerating, the group is at ~16.0x GSe NTM P/E (~55th percentile). IBank multiples typically peak early in the cycle, so GS sees limited further rerating.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker M&A backlogs translating into weaker revenue expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: Mounting LP pressure to return capital, 59% of PE unrealized value 5+ years aged and large uncommitted capital support measured sponsor M&A growth. Sponsor volumes are only up ~70% from trough.
tension_points.bear_case: Valuation disconnects and higher rates (forward curve ~90bps higher at year-end 2026, -38% correlation) limit recovery. Sept and Oct sponsor volumes fell more than 45% YoY.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued slowdown in mid-cap and sponsor M&A activity.

tension_points.bull_case: Debt maturity walls in 2028/29, higher rates, tighter financing, rising bankruptcies and AI disruption in software keep elevated activity, with 2027E restructuring revenue up 6%.
tension_points.bear_case: GS forecasts 2026E group restructuring revenue roughly flat and an easing in leveraged loan defaults per GS Credit Strategists.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Large-cap M&A and restructuring remaining weak while small-cap M&A accelerates (the FCN risk case).

theme_stances.key_argument: Most leading indicators correlated with M&A remain healthy, and M&A is still mid-cycle with substantial growth left.
Debt maturity walls, higher rates and tighter financing keep restructuring elevated, and secondaries have structural growth.
Valuation disconnects and higher rates keep sponsor M&A growth muted, though measured growth is expected.
Multiples are mid-cycle and the rally was entirely rerating, so limited further rerating is expected.
